title: Cap. IV Arg. 5 Sol close: faith is effect of εὐδοκία — Matt. 11:26; Augustine De praed. Sanct. 13, 19
pass_a_gloss: For the faith of believers, by which they are distinguished from non-believers, is not considered as an antecedent of this Divine good pleasure, but an effect, Matt. 11:26. Augustine On the Predestination of the Saints chapters 13 and 19 is to be seen. Where he accurately explains these very Pauline words which are urged by the Remonstrants.
pass_b_english: Believers' faith — what sets them off from unbelievers — is not an antecedent of this divine good pleasure but its effect (Matt. 11:26). Augustine's De praedestinatione sanctorum 13 and 19 carefully opens these very Pauline words the Remonstrants press.
source_text: Nam fides credentium, qua distinguuntur a non credentibus, non consideratur ut antecedaneum hujus Divinae εὐδοκίας, sed effectum, Matth. xi. 26. Videndus est Augustinus De Praedestinatione Sanctorum cap. 13. et 19. Ubi accurate explicat haec ipsa verba Paulina quae urgentur a Remonstrantibus.
